rule: RFC-0015 image display attributes (core/image-attrs.ts validateSize is the canonical rule): width/height must be "<n>%" in 1..100 or "<n>px" in 1..4096, CLOSED intervals. Out-of-range, non-numeric and unit-less values are DROPPED — never clamped. A block whose every attribute is invalid is not consumed at all (the literal {...} text stays). A standalone image becomes a crowiFigure (hName "figure", className "crowi-figure", align/float on the figure) with width/height on the inner image node as data-crowi-image-* hProperties.
why: data-crowi-image-* is an untrusted transport: the web re-validates every value it encounters (packages/web/src/components/editor/image-display.ts) and iOS must re-validate with the SAME value rules. This corpus fixes the drop-not-clamp rule and the duplicate-key resolution for both implementations — a client that clamps 150% to 100% renders author-visibly differently from one that drops it.
consumerContract: The api jest driver asserts the PRODUCER side (markdown → expectedAst via runPipeline with an empty registry, and storedAst/expectedAst → expectedEnvelope via sanitizeAst). The CrowiKit XCTest asserts the CONSUMER side (its sanitize-walker mirror over storedAst/expectedAst, and its strict envelope decoder over expectedEnvelope). The Swift consumer is wired up in Phase 4 (apps/apple lives on the feature-ios-app/impl branch).
exclusions: Plugin-dispatch output byte strings (Mermaid / PlantUML / link-card / shiki generated HTML) are deliberately NOT pinned by this corpus — packages/e2e/tests/renderer-plugins.spec.ts owns that coverage against a live server. The corpus pins parser/core-transform STRUCTURE and the v1 projection schema shapes only; where a stored html node value would be a generated byte string, the case either omits expectedAst (code.json) or uses a synthetic stand-in value the projection never reads (typed-nodes.json).

cases.name: figure-width-percent
cases.why: the happy path: a standalone image with a valid % width becomes crowiFigure + inner image carrying data-crowi-image-width

cases.name: figure-align-px
cases.why: layer split: align/float live on the figure’s hProperties, width/height on the inner image — never mixed

cases.name: attr-boundary-percent-valid
cases.why: closed-interval endpoints are VALID: 1% (minimum) and 100% (maximum) are both kept — a consumer rejecting either boundary violates the 1..100 closed interval

cases.name: attr-boundary-px-valid
cases.why: closed-interval endpoints are VALID: 1px (minimum) and 4096px (maximum) are both kept — a consumer rejecting either boundary violates the 1..4096 closed interval

cases.name: attr-boundary-percent-invalid
cases.why: the values ADJACENT to the % boundaries are invalid: 0% (below minimum) and 101% (above maximum) are both dropped — with zero valid attrs the block stays literal. A consumer accepting 0% or 101% over-accepts the closed interval

cases.name: attr-boundary-px-invalid
cases.why: the values ADJACENT to the px boundaries are invalid: 0px (below minimum) and 4097px (above maximum) are both dropped — with zero valid attrs the block stays literal. A consumer accepting 0px or 4097px over-accepts the closed interval

cases.name: attr-out-of-range-percent
cases.why: 150% is outside 1..100 → dropped, and with zero valid attrs the {...} block is not consumed (stays literal text, image stays inline)

cases.name: attr-out-of-range-px
cases.why: 5000px is outside 1..4096 → dropped (closed interval; 4096 itself would be valid)

cases.name: attr-non-numeric
cases.why: non-numeric values never validate → dropped, block not consumed

cases.name: attr-unit-less
cases.why: a bare number has no unit → dropped (the grammar requires % or px), block not consumed

cases.name: attr-mixed-valid-invalid
cases.why: per-value validation: the invalid width is dropped while the valid height in the same block is kept (the block IS consumed)

cases.name: attr-duplicate-last-valid-wins
cases.why: when the same key repeats with two valid values, the LAST valid occurrence wins

cases.name: attr-duplicate-invalid-repeat
cases.why: an invalid repeat does not clear an earlier valid value — 60% survives 999%
